div.head: Hn 6.1a
div.ab: Habet archiepiscopatus duos, episcopatus multos (XV), comitatus XXXII.

note.seg: multos K Co Or Gi; andere Hand darüber XV Co; XV Sc Hg [vielleicht hatte Hn: XIII, was beide Hss.-Classen, als zu ihrer Zeit falsch, änderten, oder entnahm XV aus Anm. f]
multos K Co Or Gi; another hand above it XV Co; XV Sc Hg [perhaps Hn had XIII, which both classes of MSS altered as wrong in their own time, or took XV from note f]

Benutzung eines Traktats 11. Jhs. folgt aus folg. Anm. b. Sicher enthielt Hn's Original ursprünglich eine bestimmte Zahl; letztere widersprach wohl seit den Gründungen von Ely und Carlisle der Wirklichkeit und ward daher von der Einen Hss.-Klasse durch multos [multe{h} Rs], von der anderen durch XV ersetzt, was seit 1123 richtig war. [Übrigens konnte auch der Agsächs. Traktat (s. Anm {f. k}) XV kurz vor 1027 rechnen, als Sherborn neben Ramsbury, und Crediton neben Cornwall bestand]

The use of an 11th-cent. tract follows from the next note b. Hn's original certainly contained a definite number at first; this probably no longer agreed with reality after the foundation of Ely and Carlisle, and was therefore replaced by multos [multe{h} Rs] in the one class of MSS and by XV in the other, which was correct from 1123. [Incidentally, the Anglo-Saxon tract (see note {f. k}) could also have counted XV shortly before 1027, when Sherborn existed alongside Ramsbury, and Crediton alongside Cornwall]

Davon 8 in Mercien (s. d. Gl) und in Wessex: Sussex, Surrey, Kent, Berks, Wilts, Hants, Somerset, Dorset, Devon und 15 in Denalagu (nicht 16; s. d. Gl 6). Schon im Domesday 1086 stehen gesondert Cornwall und das Land zwischen Ribble und Mersey, das spätere Lancashire; die Pipe Roll von 1130 sondert Northumberland, Heinrich von Huntingdon (ed. Arnold) Cumberland. Jedenfalls war ‘32’ um 1116 zu wenig, stammte also aus jenem älteren Traktat. S. Gl Grafschaft 4a. 8

Of these, 8 are in Mercia (see that word in Gl) and, in Wessex, Sussex, Surrey, Kent, Berks, Wilts, Hants, Somerset, Dorset, Devon, and 15 in the Danelaw (not 16; see that word in Gl 6). Already in Domesday, 1086, Cornwall and the land between Ribble and Mersey, the later Lancashire, appear separately; the Pipe Roll of 1130 separates Northumberland, and Henry of Huntingdon (ed. Arnold) Cumberland. In any case ‘32’ was too few c. 1116, and so derived from that older tract. See Gl Grafschaft 4a. 8
